Stocky closes on 31 August 2026. Your ticks save in this browser, so you can close the tab and pick up where you left off. Stocky shuts down in –– days –– hrs –– mins –– secs Stocky and the Stocky API both switch off on 31 August 2026. 17 August 2026 Stop raising new purchase orders in Stocky. Shopify's own advice — about 14 days out, so in-transit stock can still land. 31 August 2026 Stocky and the Stocky API both stop. The last day anything can read your supplier list automatically. 29 November 2026 Read-only access ends. Shopify commits to at least 90 days for downloading your data by hand. Print or save as PDF Email this to me Copy AI prompt Preview prompt Paste this into Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini. It briefs your assistant on the real deadlines and the constraints most merchants miss, then has it build a dated plan around your own store rather than a generic one. You are helping me migrate my Shopify store off the Stocky app before it shuts down on 31 August 2026. Act as a careful migration planner, not a cheerleader. First, ask me these one at a time and wait for each answer: how many suppliers I have in Stocky; how many purchase orders are currently open or in transit; whether I rely on Stocky's demand forecasting; roughly how many product vendors exist in my Shopify catalogue; and who else on my team touches Stocky day to day. Then build me a dated plan working backwards from 31 August 2026. Mark clearly which steps must happen before that date because they depend on the Stocky API, and which can slip. Hold these constraints as facts and do not contradict them: (1) Suppliers cannot be exported from Stocky at all - no CSV, no report. They are reachable only through the Stocky API, which switches off with the app, so any automated supplier migration must finish before 31 August. (2) Shopify's read-only window of at least 90 days after that date is for downloading files by hand only; it does not keep the API alive. (3) Historical purchase orders cannot be imported into Shopify - its purchase order CSV upload only adds product line items to a new draft order, losing statuses, received quantities and supplier links. Finish with two things: what I stand to lose permanently if I do nothing, and what the cheapest acceptable version of this migration looks like if I only have one working day to spend on it. That's the whole move, done. Every step ticked. Your suppliers are out, your records are archived, and someone other than you can run a normal day on the new setup. Worth printing this page for the file. Your progress 0 of 0 done Reset Stop the bleeding by 17 August Nothing else on this list works if stock is still moving through Stocky in the final fortnight. ✓ Stop raising new purchase orders in Stocky Shopify recommends drawing the line about 14 days before shutdown, so anything in transit still has time to land while Stocky can receive it. ✓ List every open and in-transit PO, and decide its fate Two choices per order: receive and close it in Stocky before the 31st, or recreate the outstanding quantity in your new system. Decide now, while there is still time to chase a supplier. ✓ Note who uses Stocky daily, and what for Receiving, counting, label printing and reordering are often four different people. The one whose job quietly depends on a Stocky report is the one who will be stuck on 1 September. Get your suppliers out by 31 August — hard deadline Do this before the CSV exports. It is the only part of the move with no manual safety net once Stocky is gone. Shopify's own migration guide puts it plainly: “Suppliers can't be exported from Stocky.” No CSV, no report, no bulk download. Every name, contact and address sits behind the Stocky API — which switches off with the app. ✓ Generate your Stocky API key and keep it safe In Stocky: Preferences → API Access. Generate one if there is not one already. This key is the only door to your supplier data, so get it well before the last-week rush. ✓ Bring your suppliers across with a tool that reads the API Anything connected to the Stocky API can do in one pass what you cannot do by hand at all. Retyping hundreds of suppliers is the single biggest time sink in this whole move. EasyScan does exactly this. Suppliers → Import from Stocky validates your key, previews every supplier, flags duplicates and any already imported, then matches them to your Shopify vendors automatically. Start your 10-day free trial → ✓ Capture the details Stocky never held cleanly While you are in there, write down lead times, minimum order quantities and payment terms for each supplier. They are not in any export, and they are what actually makes reordering work. ✓ Check the supplier count matches before you move on Compare the number in your new system against Stocky's list while both are still open. After the 31st this reconciliation is impossible. Export your records by 31 August This is your tax, audit and buying history. Treat it as an archive you are keeping — not a file you will re-import later. ✓ Export completed purchase order reports as CSV Through Stocky's reports. If your setup has no bulk export you will be downloading them one order at a time, which is exactly why this cannot wait for the final weekend. ✓ Export your stocktake history What was counted, when, by whom, and what the variance was. Nothing reconstructs this afterwards. ✓ Export historical cost data Landed costs and what you actually paid over time. This is the part accountants ask for and the part everyone forgets to save. ✓ Save any Stocky report you personally rely on Inventory value, sales by supplier, whatever you open every Monday. If a report shaped a decision, keep a copy of how it looked. ✓ Archive it somewhere that is not one person's laptop Shared drive, dated folder, one copy off that drive. You may want these files years from now, long after whoever ran the export has moved on. Worth knowing: historical purchase orders cannot be imported into Shopify. Shopify's PO CSV upload only adds product line items to a new draft order — past statuses, received quantities and supplier links do not survive the trip. These exports are records, not a restore point. Close the loop in Stocky by 31 August Leave Stocky tidy. Half-received orders are the thing that causes arguments in September. ✓ Receive and close every open, in-transit purchase order Stocky handles the receive properly and pushes the inventory to Shopify. Closing them here is far cleaner than re-keying half-received orders somewhere else. ✓ Recreate anything that will not land in time Only the outstanding quantity, not the whole order. Note the original Stocky PO number on it so the paper trail survives. ✓ Do one final inventory reconciliation against Shopify Whatever Shopify says on 1 September becomes your new opening position. Find the discrepancies while you still have Stocky's side of the story. Set up your replacement weeks before, not days These steps describe EasyScan, because it reads the Stocky API directly. The shape is the same wherever you land: connect, import, rebuild, then test with real stock. ✓ Install it and check the plan covers what you need In EasyScan, suppliers, purchase orders and stocktakes sit on Advanced or higher. Worth knowing before you start rather than mid-import. ✓ Connect Stocky in Settings → General → Integrations Enable Stocky and paste the API key from earlier. The key is validated before it saves, so a bad paste fails loudly instead of silently. ✓ Run the supplier import and read the preview properly Suppliers → Import from Stocky. The preview flags duplicates and anything already imported. Read it before confirming, not after. ✓ Match your suppliers to Shopify vendors Auto-matching walks up to 2,500 Shopify product vendors and is not resumable, so re-running will not reach the remainder. Above that ceiling the app tells you the list was partial — match the rest by hand. ✓ Rebuild your barcode label templates and test-print Print a sheet and scan it straight back with the actual scanner you use on the floor. A useful bridge: while Stocky is still running, EasyScan can print barcode labels directly from your Stocky purchase orders and stock transfers — open Reports and pick the order. No re-keying during the changeover. ✓ Add bin locations and reorder levels while you are in there Stocky never did bin locations at all. If you are rebuilding the setup anyway, this is the cheapest time to add them. Where this pays off: with sales history in place, EasyScan's Smart generate builds a purchase order for you with quantities already calculated from sales velocity, so reordering stops being a spreadsheet job. ✓ Set up your team's users, roles and permissions Not just yourself. The receiving crew needs working access on 1 September, not a support ticket. One honest limit worth planning around: a single draft purchase order caps at 500 products, splitting into up to five drafts and 2,500 items in total. Ample for most catalogues — but if Stocky's demand forecasting was the whole reason you used it, price a dedicated planning tool alongside rather than assuming a like-for-like swap. Prove it works before 31 August A migration is not done when the data is in. It is done when someone who is not you can run a normal day on it. ✓ Spot-check ten suppliers against Stocky, field by field Contact, email, address and the vendor they are linked to. Ten is enough to expose a systematic mapping error. One is not. ✓ Raise one real purchase order end to end Create it, generate the PDF, send it to a supplier who will tell you if it looks wrong, receive it, then confirm the inventory moved in Shopify. ✓ Run one real stocktake on a single location or vendor Small scope, real scanner, real staff. You are testing the workflow and the hardware, not the feature list. ✓ Have someone else do a full receive cycle unaided If it only works when you drive, you have not migrated — you have moved the bottleneck to yourself. ✓ Write the new process on one page, where the stock is Pinned up in the stockroom beats a document nobody can find. Muscle memory is what you are actually replacing. After the lights go out 1 September onwards ✓ Turn off the Stocky integration in your new app The API is gone, so the connection can only fail from here. Clearing it keeps a dead key out of your settings. ✓ Use the read-only window for anything you missed At least 90 days from 31 August, so roughly to 29 November 2026, to download data by hand. Manual exports only — nothing automated can reach in. ✓ File your exports with your tax records Leave a breadcrumb in the folder your accountant already uses. Future you will not remember a folder name from 2026. ✓ Book a review two weeks in Every migration leaves small friction that only shows up under real volume. Fix it while everyone still remembers what changed. Working through this list is a few evenings of admin. The supplier import is the part with a deadline on it — and the part EasyScan can do for you in a single pass while Stocky is still awake. Want the full picture first? See how EasyScan replaces Stocky feature by feature → Start your 10-day free trial → Questions What merchants ask about the Stocky shutdown When exactly does Stocky stop working? Stocky is unavailable after 31 August 2026, and the Stocky API stops on the same day. Shopify keeps read-only access for at least 90 days after that, to roughly 29 November 2026, but that window is for downloading files by hand only — it does not keep the API running. Can I export my suppliers from Stocky? No. Shopify's own migration guide states that suppliers cannot be exported from Stocky. There is no CSV and no report. Supplier records are reachable only through the Stocky API, so any tool that moves them for you has to finish before 31 August 2026. Will my purchase order history move to Shopify? No. Historical purchase orders cannot be imported into Shopify. Its purchase order CSV upload only adds product line items to a new draft order, so past statuses, received quantities and supplier links do not carry across. Export them as records for tax and audit instead. What should I do first? Stop raising new purchase orders in Stocky around 17 August 2026, about 14 days before shutdown, so in-transit stock can still land. Then move your suppliers out, because that is the only step with no manual fallback. Exports and setup can follow. How long does a Stocky migration take? For most stores it is a few evenings of admin spread over a fortnight. The supplier import is the only part with a hard deadline attached; exports, rebuilding labels and training the team can happen either side of it. Is this checklist free? Yes. No sign-up, no email required, and nothing is uploaded. Your ticks are stored in your own browser, so you can close the tab and pick up where you left off on the same device. Got questions?
